The evidence is inadmissible because the prosecution cannot use prior bad acts to prove propensity—that the man likely molested this child because he did so before—and it has asserted no proper non-propensity purpose such as motive, intent, or identity. Among the offered choices, the correct one is that the prosecution cannot initiate evidence of bad character in its case-in-chief, though the broader "never admissible" phrasing overstates the rule since such evidence may be admitted for proper purposes or under specific exceptions.
CONFIDENCE: 90
